title: Introduce progressive cell rendering and granular drag affordances for large data tables
creator: Amina Khatri
description: Enable a progressive, content-aware cell rendering strategy and introduce fine-grained column-edge drag affordances so very large tables feel fast, predictable, and accessible. This work touches the virtualization engine (render strategy + placeholders), UX for column resizing and reflow, keyboard accessibility, and density presets tied to tokenized spacing. Goal is to reduce jank on initial scroll, make early-visible rows meaningful, and provide discoverable, low-friction resizing interactions for power users.
acceptance_criteria: Progressive rendering implemented: first paint shows skeletons for cells in viewport; subsequent frames progressively hydrate heavy cell content without blocking scroll
Column drag affordance (0.5px expansion zone) implemented with velocity-aware snap behavior and visible guideline; works with mouse, touch, and keyboard
Resizing preserves baseline grid and does not cause content jumps or layout reflows beyond viewport row buffer
Density modes (Compact / Default / Spacious) plumbed to design tokens and available as toggles in table toolbar
Accessible announcements implemented for resize start/stop and width changes via aria-live, and keyboard resize uses arrow keys + modifiers
Unit and integration tests covering virtualization thresholds, placeholder fallback, and keyboard interactions
Performance metrics show reduction in main-thread blocking on large tables (>=1000 rows) during initial scroll by at least 30% vs baseline
design_notes: Progressive cell rendering: render DOM placeholders for the entire row quickly, then progressively mount heavier subcomponents (avatars, badges, sparklines) after first paint using rAF + requestIdleCallback where available
Use a two-tier placeholder system: low-fidelity skeleton for immediate paint, mid-fidelity content-shape placeholders for readability during hydration
Column-edge affordance: expand drag target to 14px visible hit region with a 2px neutral divider; on hover show subtle guideline and width preview tooltip
Velocity-aware snap: if user releases quickly near breakpoints (e.g., saved column widths), animate to nearest snap width to reduce micro-adjustments
Keyboard-first resize: when header is focused, support Enter to enter resize-mode, then Left/Right to nudge (1px), Shift+Arrow to nudge (10px), Esc to cancel
Density tokens: introduce table-row-height-{compact,default,spacious} and cell-padding-{compact,default,spacious} tokens; these feed both CSS variables and runtime layout calculators
Fallbacks: on older browsers without requestIdleCallback, fall back to chunked setTimeout with small yield windows
Opt-in telemetry hooks: measure mount time of first contentful cell and number of reflows per interaction for SLO monitoring
tradeoffs: Progressive hydration increases complexity in cell components (need to be idempotent) and adds more lifecycle code, but significantly improves perceived performance
Expanded drag hit targets may reduce precision for very dense column layouts; mitigated by a precision-mode toggle and keyboard resize
Adding density tokens increases theme surface area to maintain, but provides clear contract for platform teams and reduces ad-hoc CSS overrides
